title: A Survey on the Evaluation of Monosodium Glutamate (MSG) Taste in Austria
content:
This study aimed to investigate the sensory and emotional contents of the umami taste perception in a group of subjects from Austria, using a novel approach that expanded on previous findings from European samples. 
A total of 233 Austrian participants, who had lived in Austria for most of their lives, were recruited for this study. The participants underwent a blind tasting of monosodium glutamate (MSG) dissolved in water. In the first open-answer format, participants provided verbal descriptions of the solution. Then, they were instructed to rate the pleasantness of MSG and salt (NaCl) and to give basic demographic information. A text-semantic-based analysis was performed to interpret the emotional valence of the descriptors used by the participants. 
The results showed that the MSG solution was mainly received with a neutral sentiment by the entire group, as well as by both female and male subgroups. Additionally, MSG's taste and perceptual profile were delineated from the verbal descriptors. "Sour" was the most common taste descriptor, while "unfamiliar" was the most common perceptual category into which the descriptors fell. Our results also indicated that the pleasantness ratings for salt and MSG were positively correlated, suggesting that umami can produce a similar perceptual experience to salt once the unfamiliarity is overcome. 
In conclusion, our study extensively contributes to understanding umami sensory perception and its acceptance in a European group.
